content:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert -> sustained error spike on inference-eu-west. Symptoms: repeated CUDA OOMs, container CrashLoopBackOffs, autoscaler oscillation (scale-up/scale-down loop). Paging @Oncall-SRE for immediate triage.

Oncall-SRE: I'm on it, joining. Can someone grab logs for the hottest pods?

Alice M: grabbing logs now. seeing repeated `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` and some `CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED`. A lot of pods show OOMKilled and then CrashLoopBackOff.

Alice M: sample tail from model-server container:
```
2026-03-15T14:05:23Z model-server inference-7: GPU0: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
2026-03-15T14:05:26Z model-server inference-7: ERROR CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED at init_context
2026-03-15T14:05:29Z kubernetes: Pod inference-7 LastState: Terminated Reason=OOMKilled ExitCode=137
```

Bob R: looks like memory pressure on GPUs plus aggressive autoscaler settings. The HPA/cluster-autoscaler is reacting to latency, then nodes come up but pods immediately crash -> triggers scale down -> repeat. Classic capacity spiral.

Carla S: I'm cordoning the most flappy nodes (node-eu-23, node-eu-24) to stop scheduling while we diagnose.

Carla S: `kubectl cordon node-eu-23` and `kubectl cordon node-eu-24` done. Draining not yet - want to avoid mass evictions while autoscaler is noisy.

Oncall-SRE: Good call. Temporarily freeze autoscaler adjustments: patching HPA and disabling CA scale-ups for 10m.

Bob R: patch command I'm running now (will set minReplicas to current stable count and cap max to prevent runaway):
```
kubectl patch hpa inference-hpa -n inference --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":10,"maxReplicas":14}}'
# disable cluster-autoscaler scale-up via annotation (temp):
kubectl annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler redwood.io/scale-up-disabled="true" --overwrite
```

Erin K: Also routing low-memory fallback model variant for new traffic: `model: rwd-medium-quant` (smaller, int8 profile). This reduces per-request GPU allocs. I'll flip traffic on the router (10% -> fallback -> 100% if stable).

Erin K: Router commands:
```
# start gradual shift
redwoodctl route set inference-service --variant rwd-medium-quant --weight 10
# observe errors, then increase
```

Alice M: verifying impact: after cordon + HPA patch + initial 10% routing to quant variant, error rate dropped from 18% -> 7% in 3m. Latency slightly improved.

Support-Bot: Notifying affected customers: 4 enterprise customers on dedicated pools may see degraded throughput. Support ticket #INC-5934 opened and linked to this thread.

Oncall-SRE: Customer impact summary for post-incident notes: 4 enterprise customers, intermittent 5-20% 500s on /generate and embeddings, time window 14:04 - ongoing (mitigated to low rate by 14:12). Marking initial severity: sev2.

Bob R: temporary quick fixes done. Next steps: 1) keep autoscaler paused for 15m total, 2) evacuate processes from the most saturated CUDA driver version nodes (they show driver 525.*), 3) roll model-server to a pinned binary with a mem-fix if we have it.

Alice M: I see a pattern where driver mismatch + heavy KV cache + long sequences spike allocations. Proposed medium-term mitigation: enable aggressive prefix/KV caching eviction for high-latency clients and reduce default `max_context_length` for hosted route.

Carla S: I started an emergency drain plan for node-eu-25 after we ensure extra capacity in the dedicated pool. Not draining until we confirm fallback variant holds.

Oncall-SRE: Running `kubectl drain node-eu-25 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` in 3m if error rates remain <10% for two consecutive 1m windows.

Alice M: small snippet from pod describe showing CrashLoop reason:
```
Name: inference-7
State: Waiting
  Reason: CrashLoopBackOff
  Last Termination State: Terminated
    Reason: OOMKilled
    Exit Code: 137
Events:
  Normal   Pulling    2s    kubelet    Pulling image "redwood/model-server:canary"
  Warning  BackOff    1s    kubelet    Back-off restarting failed container
```

Erin K: Also disabling burst routing to hosted free tier to preserve capacity for paid customers. Adjusted rate limiters + quotas for free-tier routes.

Bob R: I've put a temporary autoscaler damping rule in place to require a 60s sustained CPU/RPS signal before scaling; that should cut oscillation. Command (cluster-autoscaler configmap):
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap cluster-autoscaler-config -p '{"data":{"scale_up_cooldown":"60s","scale_down_unneeded_time":"5m"}}'
```

Support-Bot: Support notified customers with high error rates, included workaround to use the fallback variant. Ticket updated.

PagerDuty: Incident declared. Acknowledged by Oncall-SRE.

Oncall-SRE: Current status: autoscaler limited, noisy nodes cordoned, fallback variant in rollout at 40% and error rate trending to 3-5%. Keeping thread open for next 30m. Postmortem owner: Alice M. Action items assigned: Alice - root cause and driver compatibility matrix; Bob - autoscaler tuning PR; Erin - routing safeguards; Carla - node remediation runbook.

Alice M: Adding note: collect GPU driver + CUDA versions across evicted nodes and correlate with crash times. Already grabbed `nvidia-smi -q` outputs for node-eu-23/24/25.

Carla S: I'll schedule a maintenance window to upgrade drivers on the affected hardware after the incident.

Oncall-SRE: If error rate drops below 1% and stable for 10m, we can re-enable autoscaler with safer bounds. For now keep manual controls.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigations in place. Monitoring closely.

Alice M: will kick off post-incident notes and a short blameless timeline once we confirm stability.

Erin K: thanks team. ping me if routing adjustments needed.

-- end of thread --
